title: Introduce jurisdictional assertions and conditional KMS guards
author: Nora Chen
commit_summary: 4 commits: add jurisdiction header plumbing and assertion API; implement KMS conditional guard and policy evaluator; extend RBACv2 policy to accept jurisdiction claims; add integration tests and docs; fix linting and address reviewer feedback
description: Context: Several enterprise customers in EMEA and APAC require explicit enforcement that tenant data and cryptographic operations remain bound to declared legal jurisdictions. This PR introduces a lightweight jurisdictional assertion signal that is carried alongside requests and evaluated by a new conditional KMS guard. Motivation: allow policy-driven decisions for key selection (per-tenant regional CMKs, multi-provider fallbacks) while preserving existing RBACv2 workflows and audit trail integrity. Changes: 1) Add X-Jurisdiction and internal X-Redwood-Jurisdiction assertion headers and plumbing in gateway middleware; these are validated by the new pkg/rbac/assertions subsystem which canonicalizes asserted jurisdiction claims against tenant profiles. 2) Implement pkg/kms/guard.go: a conditional guard that maps jurisdiction assertions + tenant policy -> allowed KMS providers and key aliases. The guard supports explicit deny lists, soft-fallback to a global-cmk if tenant policy allows emergency fallback, and an operator-ttl delegation path. 3) RBACv2 policy update: extend role assertions to include jurisdiction claim predicates and timebound delegations (operator TTL) that can be granted only by 'residency-admin' roles. 4) Audit: audit service now tags events with audit.jurisdiction.{tenant,claim,decision} and includes sealed metadata for non-repudiation when keys are used for encryption/decryption. 5) Feature gating & rollout: feature flag 'jurisdiction-guard' default off; rollout plan in docs/migration with a staged canary across regions. Tests & docs: unit + integration tests added, and documentation + migration notes included. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for assertion parsing and policy evaluator - [x] Integration tests for KMS selection and fallback behavior - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Security scan and static analysis - [x] Feature flag gate and Helm values entry Deployment notes: When enabling in Dedicated or Private installs, operators must supply per-tenant jurisdiction profiles (examples in examples/tenant/jurisdiction.yaml) and optionally configure KMS provider mapping in helm values. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged when feature flag is off; when enabled, requests without asserted jurisdiction use tenant default if present or proceed with existing KMS selection logic. Rollback: the flag can be disabled cluster-wide to restore prior behavior. Related work: ties to ENG-1987 (tenant residency index) and SEC-302 (audit sealing for region-bound cryptography).
review_comments: 2024-11-16 - Luis Ortega: Requested clarification on operator TTL semantics and whether delegation tokens are revocable. Action: added TTL revocation hook and tests; updated docs to call out revocation window.

2024-11-17 - Priya Raman: Suggested tightening the default fallback policy to require explicit tenant opt-in for global CMK fallback. Action: made fallback opt-in via tenant policy, kept emergency override for SRE with audit stamp.

2024-11-18 - Ethan Park: Noted potential performance impact from additional assertion validation on hot path. Action: added in-memory LRU cache for tenant jurisdiction profiles and metrics for cache hit/miss; benchmark numbers added to docs.
2024-11-19 - Nora Chen (author): Addressed feedback, ran full CI, pushed final squash commit and requested merge.
release_notes: Adds a gated feature 'jurisdiction-guard' that enables per-tenant jurisdiction assertions and a conditional KMS guard. When enabled administrators can require region-bound key usage, configure provider mappings, and obtain richer audit signals. Backwards compatible while gated. See docs/security/jurisdiction-guard.md for configuration and migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Helm: set jurisdictionGuard.enabled=true to enable. Provide tenant profiles at config map path /etc/redwood/tenants/jurisdiction.yaml or via API. Ensure KMS provider mappings are supplied under values.kms.jurisdictionMap. Monitor metric kms.guard.decision and audit.jurisdiction.* events after enabling.
risk_assessment: Low/Medium: introduces policy evaluation on request path (mitigated by caching) and cross-service header propagation. Controlled by feature flag and rollout instructions. Security review completed and SCA passed.
